reviewScope: incremental code highlighting and token caching

findings.title: Background token warming can block foreground rendering for an entire code block
findings.confirmation: code-path audit; not attributed to a captured live stall
findings.evidence: The shared language instance holds _tokenizeLock around the entire remaining TokenizeLine loop. Prewarm uses that same method. A fully reused live block still enters the lock with no lines to tokenize. Foxery calls Prewarm from its background fence warmer. The one-line maximum-wait comment does not match the critical section.
findings.fixDirection: Avoid grammar access when no tokenization is necessary; shorten the shared critical section or isolate worker grammars without breaking cross-line rule stacks.
findings.validation: Use a controlled tokenizer and synchronization signals to prove foreground cache hits do not need a background-held grammar lock; no elapsed-time assertions.
findings.validationStatus: passed final 183-test focused regression selection; no elapsed-time assertions added
findings.implementationSummary: Fully reused token sets bypass the grammar gate; warming releases shared grammar serialization at each line boundary, including alias instances.

findings.title: Setting unchanged code text destroys already styled multi-token lines
findings.fixDirection: Compare against retained lineTexts before replacing a styled Span. Preserve the rendered inline tree on no-op writes, while keeping theme changes and source-span updates correct.
findings.validation: Assert inline and text-layout identity survives identical line writes, and changed text/themes still update.
findings.validationStatus: passed final 183-test focused regression selection; no elapsed-time assertions added
findings.implementationSummary: Identical code writes retain styled inline and text-layout identity. Theme/language/re-registered-theme changes force clean restyling, including single-style runs; mutable external edits retain a conservative path.

findings.title: A table height change remeasures unchanged cells at two widths
findings.fixDirection: Retain natural/min-content metrics with explicit content/style invalidation, and avoid alternating stable cells between infinite and fitted constraints on a height-only change.
findings.validation: Count actual MeasureOverride executions for unchanged cells; retain wrapping, span, font/theme, and resizing coverage. A same-sized child invalidation alone already avoids the extra work.
findings.validationStatus: passed final 183-test focused regression selection; no elapsed-time assertions added
findings.implementationSummary: Natural metrics and lazy min-content floors are retained for observable Markdown cells; width changes rewrap once and stable cells keep their final measure. Content/typography/chrome/structure invalidation and observer teardown are covered. Unsupported custom or embedded-control cells keep the conservative path.

findings.title: Incremental highlighting still scans the full line prefix
findings.fixDirection: Carry the earliest dirty line from CodeBlock into the token/formatting pipeline, retaining rule-stack propagation and invalidating appropriately for text replacement and theme changes.
findings.validation: Assert prefix read/visit counts remain bounded for append-only updates and compare styled output for multiline grammar states. Existing tokenization already reuses prefix tokens; the remaining issue is scans and collection bookkeeping.
findings.validationStatus: passed final 183-test focused regression selection; no elapsed-time assertions added
findings.implementationSummary: CodeBlock supplies authoritative dirty-tail and fixed-chunk hints, preserving owned token prefixes and formatting only affected suffixes. Exposed mutable collections fall back safely; trimming and deferred styling checks also respect dirtiness.
findings.scopeAfterFix: The authoritative CodeBlock pipeline is bounded; callers supplying arbitrary mutable collections without dirtiness hints intentionally retain safe prefix validation.

findings.title: The shared token cache flushes all entries at capacity and has no aggregate byte/character budget
findings.fixDirection: Use bounded least-recently-used eviction with text/token retention weights and oversized-entry handling. Keep hot snippets when new background-warmed snippets arrive.
findings.validation: Retain a repeatedly used entry while inserting other entries past capacity; enforce weight/count caps without a full-cache cliff.
findings.validationStatus: passed final 183-test focused regression selection; no elapsed-time assertions added
findings.implementationSummary: Shared tokens use a thread-safe weighted LRU: 1024-entry cap, 16 MiB estimated retention weight, 512 KiB per-entry admission weight. Entries are immutable before publication; overflow evicts old entries individually.

findings.title: Unchanged active-search refreshes rebuild match collections despite memo hits
findings.scope: Requires an active search. No direct ApplyTextSearch callers were found in current Foxery source, so this is a library optimization rather than evidence for the current app lag. Allocations include the complete refresh/layout path, not solely the dictionaries.
findings.fixDirection: Retain aggregate results when ordered blocks and memo results are unchanged; update changed blocks without rebuilding every match collection.
findings.validation: Assert unchanged refresh preserves the match result collection and performs zero rematches; changing queries, content, block order, and highlights must stay correct.
findings.validationStatus: passed final 183-test focused regression selection; no elapsed-time assertions added
findings.implementationSummary: Unchanged ordered blocks/memos/highlights retain the aggregate match collection and emit no replacement notification. Ownership-aware highlights and globally distinct matcher generations keep moved blocks correct; spare collections retain capacity without retired-block references.

findings.title: RAM image-cache wrapper has no strong owner and disappears across GC
findings.scope: Image-bearing Markdown. Weak retention is intentional in the current API, but the wrapper is not held even by a live returned cache reader.
findings.fixDirection: Offer bounded strong retention, or make weak lifetime follow an actually retained object. Preserve HTTP freshness, no-store, and stream ownership semantics.
findings.validation: Prove small reusable entries survive expected GC cycles within budget; verify eviction releases bytes/metadata and honors HTTP validators.
findings.validationStatus: passed final 183-test focused regression selection; no elapsed-time assertions added
findings.implementationSummary: RAM image bytes have strong LRU retention under per-instance 64 MiB / 128-entry defaults. Readers own independent streams/metadata; validators, no-store, cancellation, replacement and budget changes remain correct.

findings.title: Image-cache entry size is checked after fully buffering the source
findings.fixDirection: Reject oversized seekable sources before copying; bound buffering of unknown-length sources. Retain the documented nonpositive-limit behavior.
findings.validation: Count bytes read and allocation shape for oversized seekable/nonseekable streams, plus cancellation and no-store cases.
findings.validationStatus: passed final 183-test focused regression selection; no elapsed-time assertions added
findings.implementationSummary: Seekable oversized sources are rejected before reading. Unknown-length reads stop at limit+1 bytes; aggregate limits still bound writes if the per-entry cap is disabled.

notes: No full suite or long benchmark run was started.
These are optimization opportunities, not an attribution of current live-app stalls.
Full text construction for explicit copy operations was not counted as unnecessary background work.
Existing incremental parsing, token reuse, shaped-run caching, and lazy text projections were considered rather than rediscovered as missing features.
executionNotes: Fixes started with LM-PERF-01/02 and LM-PERF-03; independent image/search work proceeds alongside them.

Baseline 92-test selection: 91 passed, one pre-existing unrequested-projection allocation-ratio assertion failed (11,187 versus 7,192 bytes). Replace that guard with exact per-renderer block-collection/projection-build work assertions and retain allocations as an explicit report.
completionNotes: All eight checklist items are implemented and covered by deterministic regressions.
Baseline allocation-ratio failure was replaced by direct block-walk/projection-build invariants; original allocation measurement remains an explicit report.
Validation used focused regressions and small audit probes, not the full suite or a long benchmark matrix. Package publication is separate from this fix set.
Compatibility paths deliberately remeasure unsupported custom/embedded table cells and validate arbitrary externally exposed inline collections.

repeatableBenchmark.validation: Two sequential original/optimized Release pairs passed all six workloads; five deterministic comparator tests passed. Historical source and dependencies were unchanged; only the identical harness was copied into the original worktree.
repeatableBenchmark.scope: Warm-cache synchronous UI work, allocations and timings; does not measure retained/native memory, background work, cold start or GPU presentation.
repeatableBenchmark.historicalCompatibility: Optional counters bind outside measurements; unavailable historical counters are JSON null and are never interpreted as zero.

originalComparison.interpretation: Targeted allocation and table work reductions repeated in both pairs. Width-change and construction timing differences changed sign between pairs; no speedup claimed for those controls. Timings remain observations, not gates.
originalComparison.provenance: Dirty markers reflect benchmark-only changes. Original tracked source/configuration matched f8e0fd3; optimized product source matched e4d6f49b. Harness/headless-host bytes and report environments matched across both worktrees.
